Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 12-May-2025 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  Manipal Institute of Technology, Bengaluru  
  BTech VI Semester  
  End Semester Examination - April / May -2025  
  AI for Medical Image Analysis [CSE-4011]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                                                                                                                       (5)  
  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Analyse how domain knowledge is applied differently in hierarchical segmentation versus                (3)  
  foreground segmentation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)           Explain the difference between push and pull modes of image transfer and how each affects              (2)  
  network efficiency and clinical workflow.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2)                Describe the main steps in Mahapatra et al.'s active learning process for image segmentation,         (4)  
  including how the initial model is trained, how uncertainty and diversity guide sample selection, and  
  A)           how a conditional GAN is used to enhance the labelled dataset before retraining.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           Analyse the importance of annotated imaging datasets in building effective machine learning            (3)  
  models for radiology, and explore the factors that influence their reliability and availability.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  Page 1 of 3

C)         Analyse the role of intensity comparisons in the BRIEF descriptor and explain how they contribute to (3)  
  efficient keypoint matching.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)               How can domain knowledge about boundary appearance be applied to improve the segmentation               (5)  
  of a foreground object with unclear boundaries in an ultrasound image using methods such as  
  A)         active contours or level sets?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Apply the concept of temporal continuity to describe how you would segment a 4D (3D+ Time) MRI (5)  
  heart sequence consistently across multiple time steps.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)               Analyse how the use of both spatial and contextual encoding paths in the Dual Encoding U-Net            (5)  
  architecture enables the model to balance local detail preservation with global context  
  A)         understanding for effective retinal vessel segmentation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Analyse how the initial low-resolution classification step in the coarse-to-fine ML-assisted tumour     (5)  
  detection pipeline contributes to the overall efficiency of the framework. Why is it critical to the  
  system's performance?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)               Analyse the architectural differences between TensorFlow and Caffe and discuss how these                (5)  
  differences impact their use in designing deep learning models for medical image segmentation.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Explain how organizing radiology data in a consistent and standardized format can help in the           (3)  
  development of machine learning applications.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)         Explain why a multivariate normal distribution is commonly used for modelling feature vectors.          (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"
